newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends off, trade lifts from lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends off, trade lifts from lows.

text.p: Steady shortcovering by the trade and new fund buying lifted CSCE world sugar futures off the lows hit early, but late-session trade selling kept prices below unchanged by the close, dealers said.

Prices fell in early dealings on trade and then speculative selling. By midday, the market had begun to recoup losses with the most-active May contract lingering around its previous downside target of 11.00 cents.

Fresh fund buying pushed the most-active May contract over the key level to settle at 11.10 cents a lb, down 0.06 cent. March ended 0.15 lower at 11.18, while the back months finished unchanged to down 0.03.
Volume was estimated at 41,521 lots compared with Thursday's official volume of 48,826 lots.
The March/May spread narrowed to 0.08 compared with 0.17 Thursday.
Open interest in the May contract rose by 8,595 lots to 61,494 lots from Thursday. Open interest in March fell 6,801 lots to 25,548 lots.
The last trading day for the spot month is February 28.
Despite late-session gains, market sources expect prices to continue their downward momentum.
"The market probably has a chance of pulling back to the 10.70s in the next week or two," a broker said, adding that the speculators are net long by about 30,000 contracts.
Support in May was seen at 10.85 cents, Wednesday's low, and resistance at today's high of 11.18 cents.
